stanzas.sanskrit:
रामेऽथ गोकुलगते प्रमदाप्रसक्ते
हूतानुपेतयमुनादमने मदान्धे ।
स्वैरं समारमति सेवकवादमूढो
दूतं न्ययुङ्क्त तव पौण्ड्रकवासुदेवः ॥ ८३-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Balarama went to Gokula and had great time with Gopikas. He changed the course of river Yamuna when it did not oblige to his invite. At that time Paundraka Vaasudeva misled by the ill advice of his subordinates, sent a messenger to Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rāme’tha gokulagate pramadāprasakte
hūtānupetayamunādamane madāndhe |
svairaṃ samāramati sevakavādamūḍho
dūtaṃ nyayuṅkta tava pauṇḍrakavāsudevaḥ || 83-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
नारायणोऽहमवतीर्ण इहास्मि भूमौ
धत्से किल त्वमपि मामकलक्षणानि ।
उत्सृज्य तानि शरणं व्रज मामिति त्वां
दूतो जगाद सकलैर्हसितः सभायाम् ॥ ८३-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Paundraka Vaasudeva sent a messenger conveying that he is the Mahavishnu descended on this earth and that Krishna bears his emblems. He commanded that Krishna give those to him and surrender to him. The courtiers on hearing the message laughed and made fun of it.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nārāyaṇo’hamavatīrṇa ihāsmi bhūmau
dhatse kila tvamapi māmakalakṣaṇāni |
utsṛjya tāni śaraṇaṃ vraja māmiti tvāṃ
dūto jagāda sakalairhasitaḥ sabhāyām || 83-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दूतेऽथ यातवति यादवसैनिकैस्त्वं
यातो ददर्शिथ वपुः किल पौण्ड्रकीयम् ।
तापेन वक्षसि कृताङ्कमनल्पमूल्य-
-श्रीकौस्तुभं मकरकुण्डलपीतचेलम् ॥ ८३-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: After the messenger left, Krishna went with the Yadava army to meet Paundraka. Paundraka's chest was marked by a burnt sign Srivatsam, expensive kausthubam around his neck, fish shaped ear drops and a yellow silk garment.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dūte’tha yātavati yādavasainikaistvaṃ
yāto dadarśitha vapuḥ kila pauṇḍrakīyam |
tāpena vakṣasi kṛtāṅkamanalpamūlya-
-śrīkaustubhaṃ makarakuṇḍalapītacelam || 83-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कालायसं निजसुदर्शनमस्यतोऽस्य
कालानलोत्करकिरेण सुदर्शनेन ।
शीर्षं चकर्तिथ ममर्दिथ चास्य सेनां
तन्मित्र काशिपशिरोऽपि चकर्थ काश्याम् ॥ ८३-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: On seeing Krishna, he threw the Sudharshana chakra on Bhagwan. Immediately, Krishna retaliated with HIS Sudharshana Chakra emitting fire sparks and cut his head off. Krishna destroyed the army and cut the head of King of Kasi and made it fall in the land of Kashi itself.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kālāyasaṃ nijasudarśanamasyato’sya
kālānalotkarakireṇa sudarśanena |
śīrṣaṃ cakartitha mamarditha cāsya senāṃ
tanmitra kāśipaśiro’pi cakartha kāśyām || 83-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
जाड्येन बालकगिराऽपि किलाहमेव
श्रीवासुदेव इति रूढमतिश्चिरं सः ।
सायुज्यमेव भवदैक्यधिया गतोऽभूत्
को नाम कस्य सुकृतं कथमित्यवेयात् ॥ ८३-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Paundraka was foolish to consider himself as Vaasudeva. But this thought made him constantly be in oneness with Bhagwan and so he attained Moksham. No one can say whose good deeds will lead him to where?!
stanzas.stanza_roman:
jāḍyena bālakagirā’pi kilāhameva
śrīvāsudeva iti rūḍhamatiściraṃ saḥ |
sāyujyameva bhavadaikyadhiyā gato’bhūt
ko nāma kasya sukṛtaṃ kathamityaveyāt || 83-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
काशीश्वरस्य तनयोऽथ सुदक्षिणाख्यः
शर्वं प्रपूज्य भवते विहिताभिचारः ।
कृत्यानलं कमपि बाणरणातिभीतै-
-र्भूतैः कथञ्चन वृतैः सममभ्यमुञ्चत् ॥ ८३-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Sudhakshinan, son of King of Kashi, a great devotee of Lord Shiva acquired some black magic powers & sent an evil fire called Krityaa over Krishna. He also took the support of bhoothaganaas who ran away when Krishna fought with Banasura.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kāśīśvarasya tanayo’tha sudakṣiṇākhyaḥ
śarvaṃ prapūjya bhavate vihitābhicāraḥ |
kṛtyānalaṃ kamapi bāṇaraṇātibhītai-
-rbhūtaiḥ kathañcana vṛtaiḥ samamabhyamuñcat || 83-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तालप्रमाणचरणामखिलं दहन्तीं
कृत्यां विलोक्य चकितैः कथितोऽपि पौरैः ।
द्यूतोत्सवे किमपि नो चलितो विभो त्वं
पार्श्वस्थमाशु विससर्जिथ कालचक्रम् ॥ ८३-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The frightened people saw the Krityaa fire with long legs like palm trees burning everything and they informed Bhagwan. Krishna who was playing a game of dice, effortlessly sent the Sudharshana chakra.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tālapramāṇacaraṇāmakhilaṃ dahantīṃ
kṛtyāṃ vilokya cakitaiḥ kathito’pi pauraiḥ |
dyūtotsave kimapi no calito vibho tvaṃ
pārśvasthamāśu visasarjitha kālacakram || 83-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अभ्यापतत्यमितधाम्नि भवन्महास्त्रे
हा हेति विद्रुतवती खलु घोरकृत्या ।
रोषात् सुदक्षिणमदक्षिणचेष्टितं तं
पुप्लोष चक्रमपि काशिपुरीमधाक्षीत् ॥ ८३-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s brilliant great weapon dashed towards Krityaa. The terrible Krityaa ran away and started to attack Sudakshina who impressed it initially and burnt him and city of Kashi to ashes.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
abhyāpatatyamitadhāmni bhavanmahāstre
hā heti vidrutavatī khalu ghorakṛtyā |
roṣāt sudakṣiṇamadakṣiṇaceṣṭitaṃ taṃ
puploṣa cakramapi kāśipurīmadhākṣīt || 83-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
स खलु विविदो रक्षोघाते कृतोपकृतिः पुरा
तव तु कलया मृत्युं प्राप्तुं तदा खलतां गतः ।
नरकसचिवो देशक्लेशं सृजन् नगरान्तिके
झटिति हलिना युध्यन्नद्धा पपात तलाहतः ॥ ८३-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: During thretha yuga, when Bhagwan took the incarnation as Rama, Dvividha was helpful in killing of Ravana. But during incarnation as Krishna, he was born with bad virtues and was minister in Narakasuran's kingdom. He aided Narakasuran in doing mischief to the people of Dwaraka. Balaraman killed Vividha effortlessly and he fell down dead.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sa khalu vivido rakṣoghāte kṛtopakṛtiḥ purā
tava tu kalayā mṛtyuṃ prāptuṃ tadā khalatāṃ gataḥ |
narakasacivo deśakleśaṃ sṛjan nagarāntike
jhaṭiti halinā yudhyannaddhā papāta talāhataḥ || 83-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
साम्बं कौरव्यपुत्रीहरणनियमितं सान्त्वनार्थी कुरूणां
यातस्तद्वाक्यरोषोद्धृतकरिनगरो मोचयामास रामः ।
ते घात्याः पाण्डवेयैरिति यदुपृतनां नामुचस्त्वं तदानीं
तं त्वां दुर्बोधलीलं पवनपुरपते तापशान्त्यै निषेवे ॥ ८३-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Saamba, Jambavathi's son tried to abduct Lakshmanai, Duryodanan's daughter and was caught and tied by Kauravas. Balaraam went to the Kauravas to pacify them but was enraged by their talks and lifted up Hastinaapur and released Saamba. Krishna did not send his Yadavas army to kill kauravas then, as HE waited for Pandavas to kill them.
Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan, whose leelas cannot be understood easily by all and pleaded protection from all his afflictions.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sāmbaṃ kauravyaputrīharaṇaniyamitaṃ sāntvanārthī kurūṇāṃ
yātastadvākyaroṣoddhṛtakarinagaro mocayāmāsa rāmaḥ |
te ghātyāḥ pāṇḍaveyairiti yadupṛtanāṃ nāmucastvaṃ tadānīṃ
taṃ tvāṃ durbodhalīlaṃ pavanapurapate tāpaśāntyai niṣeve || 83-10 ||
